reviewed: module.json (full walk of nodes S1.gate to S7.wrap)

segments.reason: Probe first, then a sure-noted refutation with a time-to-death rule; skip lanes at S1.gate_ok and S1.talk_ok; S1.deep_prehosp handles the MARCH conflict without a new trap.
Three-peak probes where each wrong option is a named trap (TR30, TR1) and the why-nodes separate peaks by timing; S2.close recaps cleanly.
Vignettes carry the airway traps (TR2, TR22) with GCS and age as qualifiers; S3.p2_p and S3.p3_p are short, and their partial options lack a Show-me exit.

Largest segment with strong contrast probes, but about thirteen explain nodes (S4.pair_why, S4.tp_next_why, S4.flail_cause_why and others) exit only to Try again on the same stem; S4.not_list asks about a list the learner has not been shown.
Worked case, then fade ladder with a skip lane; S5.why_t9, S5.fade1_t9a and S5.fade4_t4a name the wrong model, and each fade probe has a Show-me exit to the mechanism.

Management run: about a dozen wrong-answer nodes are a bare 'That choice is not right.' plus one line with Try again only; S6.peer_t10 and S6.peer_t27 mark correct steps as wrong with no corrected figure; S6.wx packs four steps into three messages.

Twelve cold stems in a row with no interleaving; most re-ask beliefs already corrected in S1 to S6, two- and three-option stems are guessable, and S7.open promises an answer control that does not exist.

best_parts: node S1.gate_t1a with S1.why_gate: sure_note names the wrong model (loudest problem first), then the time-to-death rule is taught before the probe is repeated.
nodes S4.ppv_t5 and S4.ppv_why: a predict-then-show mechanism for positive pressure in a one-way valve, with the trap named and a Show-me exit.

nodes S5.why_t9, S5.fade1_t9a and S5.fade1_show: worked case, then a faded probe with three wrong models each mapped to its own trap (TR9), and an explanation that names the pulse before the pressure.
nodes S4.site_adult_t11a and S4.site_child_t11: both exam keys are set side by side and the age split is named as the rule to keep, which is the exam-form repair the trap map asks for.
flaws: node S6.peer_t10: step 1 (warmed 1 L crystalloid, then blood) is the current ATLS figure taught in S6.wx and S6.fluid_ok, yet the node says 'That choice is not right' and then that a correct 1 L step 'can look like the error'. The learner gets a contradictory signal, no corrected dose, no Show-me exit, and no repair for TR10 (R2, R9).

node S6.peer_t27: step 3 (TXA within 3 h, then 1 g over 8 h) is correct as taught in S6.txa_ok, yet is flagged wrong. The feedback says only 'Separate the start window from the infusion' with Try again and no Show-me exit (R2, R5).

nodes S6.brain_t18, S6.cath_t23, S6.cath2_t23, S6.child_t22, S6.site_t11, S6.site_t3, S6.pair_t11, S6.flail_t14, S6.txa_t27, S6.fluid_t10, S6.ssurvey_t2: wrong-answer feedback opens with a bare 'That choice is not right.' and offers only Try again. The trap is named in one sentence and no second explanation is offered (R5, R8). The sim shows the 2 L belief survives S6.peer_t10 and changes only on the second miss at S6.fluid_t10.
node S6.wx: four numbered steps across three messages, with steps 3 and 4 packed into one message. The worked plan is hard to hold in one read (R4).
node S4.not_list: 'Which is NOT one of them?' is asked before the five injuries are listed; the list appears only in S4.not_list_why after a miss. The first answer is a guess from memory (R4, R5).

nodes S4.pair_why, S4.tp_next_why, S4.flail_cause_why, S4.mediast_why, S4.right_pair_why, S4.tamp_why, S4.site_adult_why, S4.site_child_why, S4.circ_why, S4.not_list_why, S4.ppv_why, S4.tp_dx_why, S4.flail_mgmt_why: each explanation exits only to Try again on the same stem, so the explanation never moves the learner forward. This is a forced retest with no progression (R5).

node S4.site_adult_t11a: two exam keys are set side by side with 'hold both keys', but there is no rule for which key a given exam uses. The learner is left with two answers and no decision rule (R6).

node S7.open: promises 'you can ask for the answer', but no stem in S7 offers an answer control. It also says hints are offered on the first four only, yet S7.p3 has none and S7.p1, S7.p2, S7.p4 do (R8, R4).

nodes S7.p3, S7.p10, S7.p11: two choices each, so a guess is a coin flip. Each has a longer option that is the trap in S7.p3 and S7.p10, so the choice rests on one remembered rule with no second distractor to test it (R2).

segment S7 as a whole: twelve stems in a row with no interleaved teaching, and most re-ask a belief already corrected earlier (S7.p2 repeats S1.talk, S7.p4 repeats S3.p3, S7.p5 repeats S4.tp_next, S7.p7 repeats S4.mediast). It reads as repetition more than transfer (R2, R4, R8).

report.json (trap and objective texts): wording is template-level; traps are reported as fell_recovered or avoided by first encounter only, so a retry-only fall (TR27 at the S6.peer retry) is reported as avoided. The objective tiers do not reflect the 9/9 cold quiz result in the misconceived walk (R9).

report_check.headline: The mixed headline does not match the misconceived walk: all 20 traps were refuted and retested, and 9 of 9 cold stems were correct. The headline should say which qualifier to fix first and mention the cold-quiz result.
report_check.objectives: Objective tiers use template wording and do not differentiate between a learner who recovered on the cold quiz and one who did not (R9).
report_check.traps: Traps report first encounter only. Retry-only falls (TR18 at S6.brain_t18, TR27 at S6.peer_t27) are not distinguished from clean corrections (R9).
report_check.calibration: overconfident is named from the sure-wrong count, which is accurate. The guess-right count is not reflected (minor).
report_check.next_steps: Ordering is useful: confident errors first, then gaps, then shaky, with one concrete action.

sim_check.misconceived: The path separates each wrong model at the point of choice for S1 to S5, and the report names the model back. Friction in S6 (retry-only feedback, the S6.peer_t10 contradiction) means a learner holding the 2 L belief can finish the module without a repair they can use. The sim's own verdict was engagement 3 of 5, and the S7 quiz is the weakest stretch of the path.
sim_check.fixes_needed: Put the corrected figure in the wrong-answer line itself (S6.peer_t10, S6.peer_t27). Add a Show-me exit to every S6 wrong node. Give each S4 explanation a forward move after it.

merge_ideas: Take S5's worked case then fade structure, with its explanation-then-retest exits, and apply it to S6: a worked plan first, then one faded probe per step, each with a Show-me exit.

Replace S6.peer_t10 with a node that says step 1 is the ATLS 10th figure and names the 2 L belief as the wrong model, then gives the reason (large volumes dilute clotting factors and cool the patient) before the retest.
Move the five life-threatening chest injuries above S4.not_list so the NOT question tests recall of a list the learner has just seen.
Interleave S7: alternate fresh stems with one short teach per two stems, and add a cold stem for TR3 and TR5 earlier so the quiz does not run twelve probes with the same keys.
Make the report objective tier depend on the path: refuted then recovered on the cold quiz is secure, refuted then fell again is shaky, and name the qualifier to fix first in the headline.
unscored_notes: Not gated. No typing and no run-time model; every node has a forward path, and the skip lanes at S1.gate_ok, S2.open_ok, S5.why_ok and S6.case lead to the correct next node. Facts are not judged (CLAUDE.md). The claims section of module.json was not walked beyond the node text it supports.
